name: Perella Weinberg Partners
reason: Advisory boutique whose earnings are set by M&A/restructuring activity; GAAP EPS negative 2020-2024 and only $0.47 in 2025 with adjusted-vs-GAAP gap of 45%, no forecastable base.

name: Ameris Bancorp
reason: Southeast bank whose 16.8% EPS CAGR came with share count up 7.9%/yr (acquisition-driven) plus mortgage/warehouse lines tied to the rate cycle; ordinary regional bank with no specialness.

name: T-Mobile US, Inc.
reason: Share-taking member of a 3-player US wireless oligopoly with EBIT margin up from 6.5% to 21% over 10y, adj EPS $0.82 to $9.72 and heavy buybacks (4.4x FCF over 10y); net debt/EBITDA 3.6x is fine for a defensive subscription business, though watch price competition and cable MVNOs.

name: Innoviva, Inc.
reason: Royalty stream on GSK's Relvar/Anoro faces generic erosion (consensus EPS -27% FY1, LTG ~1%), and the pivot into owned specialty-pharma assets is unproven.

name: Energy Transfer LP
reason: Midstream MLP with commodity/NGL marketing exposure, EPS flat over 10y (CAGR 0.9%) while units rose 12.5%/yr and net debt/EBITDA is 4.6x.

name: Halozyme Therapeutics, Inc.
reason: ENHANZE royalty platform has superb economics (EBIT margin 58%, EPS 0.98x peak) but faces MDASE patent expiries, the Keytruda subQ patent fight with Merck and acquisition-led diversification (acq/FCF 1.0x), so 10-year royalties cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: LKQ Corporation
reason: Roll-up parts distributor (acq/FCF 0.69x over 10y) with EPS down from $3.96 (2021) to $3.01, weak Europe, net debt/EBITDA 3.1x and long-run EV threat to mechanical parts.

name: Genworth Financial, Inc.
reason: Legacy long-term-care book with ROE averaging 3.1% and EPS at 0.24x its 10y high; earnings depend on LTC reserve and rate actions plus a mortgage-insurance stake.

name: ARMOUR Residential REIT, Inc.
reason: Levered agency-MBS mortgage REIT driven entirely by rates and spreads; per-share earnings fell from $18.74 to $3.06 over 10y while shares rose 27%/yr.

name: Perrigo Company PLC
reason: OTC/store-brand maker with EPS down from $6.39 to $2.75 over the decade, negative 10y average ROIC, acq/FCF 1.16x and net debt/EBITDA 4.8x.

name: Piper Sandler Companies
reason: Investment bank/broker whose earnings swing with capital-markets activity (EPS $5.48 in 2021 to $2.32 in 2023); EBIT margin now in its 91st percentile.

name: Sunoco LP
reason: Fuel distributor with fuel-margin and inventory-price exposure, acquisition-driven growth (acq/FCF 1.85x), units up 10.6%/yr and net debt/EBITDA 8.6x.

name: Portland General Electric Company
reason: Regulated Oregon utility with 10y EPS CAGR of 4.1%, net debt/EBITDA 4.6x, negative FCF and western wildfire-liability risk; no special route to 7%+ EPS growth.

name: Las Vegas Sands Corp.
reason: Macau/Singapore integrated resorts with EPS still below 2018 and losses in 2020-2022; results depend on Chinese policy, the Macau concession regime and VIP/mass demand that cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Hercules Capital, Inc.
reason: Venture-debt BDC whose earnings depend on the credit cycle and floating rates; shares rose 10.5%/yr and consensus sees flat EPS through FY3.

name: Happen, Inc.
reason: Former LendingClub, a consumer unsecured lender and marketplace whose EPS swung from -$1.53 to $2.79 to $0.36 with the credit and funding cycle; FY1-3 growth relies on a credit recovery.

name: Dolby Laboratories, Inc.
reason: High-quality licensing franchise with net cash and buybacks, but revenue grew only 3.3%/yr over 10y; 7%+ EPS growth needs Atmos/Vision/imaging adoption to beat device-unit cycles and open-codec competition, which is hard to underwrite.

name: Prestige Consumer Healthcare Inc
reason: Portfolio of niche #1 OTC brands with EBIT margin steady at about 30% for a decade, adj EPS CAGR 7.3% with only one down year (-3% in 2025) and net debt/EBITDA down to 2.9x; low-single-digit organic growth plus ~10% FCF yield on buybacks/deleveraging gives a plausible 7%+ route.

name: Molson Coors Beverage Company
reason: Mainstream beer brands in structural volume decline, 10y EPS CAGR 3.7%, 10y average ROIC 2.2% and consensus EPS -13.5% FY1; cheap but not special.

name: Western Alliance Bancorp
reason: Fast-growing commercial bank (EPS CAGR 15.7%, ROE avg 16.3%) but funded by concentrated, rate-sensitive deposits (EPS fell 33% in the 2023 deposit run) and exposed to mortgage warehouse and CRE.
